newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel debt seen little moved by fire.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel debt seen little moved by fire.

text.p: LONDON, November 19 (LPC) - Eurotunnel bank debt bid levels were little moved at about 39.5 percent as the smoke cleared from a fire in the undersea Channel Tunnel link Monday night, according to debt traders.
"I don't think this has moved the market for the debt," said one debt market analyst.

"The value of the debt is based on fundamental cash flow analysis. I can't see that a 24-hour shutdown is going to have much of an impact. The more worrying aspect is the bad impression this may create," he said.

Distressed bank debt investors will be less impressed by the fire's immediate impact because, under the terms of the restructuring currently mooted, they face such a long wait until they are paid in full.

"A debt investor will be concerned with the prospects for cash flows in about 2003,'' the analyst said. Unless the damage proves to be more severe the fire is not likely to have a strong effect on bank debt prices, he added.
